formula_checks.name: theLookBack
formula_checks.why: Passing the amount, the two histories, the months and today straight to lookBack and returning its answer unchanged is right for an orchestrator: the screen computes nothing, the three figures (MK-PF-M-010, -011, -012) all come from one answer, so the difference always equals moved − stayed. It inherits lookBack's price-only measurement (finding on MK-PF-F-023). The owner rule DEC-0233 is about layout only.

formula_checks.name: lookBack
formula_checks.why: The arithmetic is right: end value = amount × factor, change = end − amount, percent = (factor − 1) × 100, difference = moved − stayed, refusing unless the amount is above zero and both factors exist. The percent is a percent, as the batch note says. It is incomplete in what it measures: it uses prices only, so distributions are left out. Comparing a stock fund with a bond fund (which pays most of its return as distributions) over a year understates the bond fund by its yield, and the difference shown is wrong in money. The author's rule says the screen says 'price changes only', which discloses it but does not make the dollar difference right; owner decision Q16 asks for time-weighted total returns.
formula_checks.should_be: Factor = the fund's total-return factor over the window (closes adjusted for distributions, i.e. distributions reinvested); the rest unchanged.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision Q16 (time-weighted return); standard practice that a fund's return includes its distributions.

formula_checks.name: factorOverMonths
formula_checks.why: Latest close ÷ the last close on or before the cut-off, refusing when the record does not reach the cut-off or the start close is not above zero, is right — and better than MK-PF-F-010 / MK-PF-F-029, which fall back. But 'today moved back the given number of months' does not say what happens when that month is shorter. MK-PF-F-008 and MK-NW-F-090 both stop at the month's last day (owner decision DEC-3768b: one month before 31 March is 28 February). A plain month subtraction overflows instead (31 March − 1 month → 3 March), which on the look-back screen would measure a different window from the period chips.
formula_checks.should_be: Cut-off = today moved back the given number of months, stopping at that month's last day when it is shorter (as MK-PF-F-008 / MK-NW-F-090).
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision DEC-3768b; agreement with MK-PF-F-008 and MK-NW-F-090.

formula_checks.name: startDateFor
formula_checks.why: Moving back whole months and stopping at the month's last day when that month is shorter is the right calendar rule (owner decision DEC-3768b), and 1 January for This year is right. It agrees with MK-NW-F-090 for every label both share. Low: for an unknown label this card gives today and MK-NW-F-090 gives 12 months back; here the input is typed as one of the six periods, so it cannot reach a screen. MK-PF-F-022 (factorOverMonths) does not state the month-end rule at all — that finding is on that card.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision DEC-3768b (batch note); agreement with MK-NW-F-090.

formula_checks.name: latestClose
formula_checks.why: The most recent close is right in idea, but 'the close of the last price on record' means the last item in the list, which is the latest only when the list is sorted oldest first. Nothing on the card sorts it or says it must arrive sorted, and a price history from a broker or data feed is often newest first. Then this returns the OLDEST close, and every market value, gain and return built on it is wrong.
formula_checks.should_be: The close of the price with the latest date (whatever order the list is in); nothing when there are no prices.

formula_checks.name: periodReturn
formula_checks.why: Three faults. (1) The start is the close on or before the period's FIRST day, so the first day's own move is left out. Owner decision Q3 puts both edge days inside the period, and MK-NW-O-008 reads its beginning at the day BEFORE the period opens (the author records fixing exactly this there, B-115); the holding rows and the portfolio return then disagree by one day's move. (2) When the prices do not reach the period's start it falls back to the first close and labels a shorter span with the period's name (a 1Y return that is really five months) — MK-PF-F-022 refuses in the same case, MK-PF-F-034 has no fallback. (3) Years for the yearly rate are days ÷ 365.25, while MK-NW-O-008 uses days ÷ 365. Turning 2Y into a yearly rate and keeping 1Y as a total is right.
formula_checks.should_be: Start = the close on or before the day before the period's first day; refuse when there is none. Return = end ÷ start − 1. For 2Y, the yearly rate (end ÷ start)^(1/2) − 1. Use the same day count for years as MK-NW-O-008.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision Q3 (both edge days inside); MK-NW-O-008 (beginning read the day before); agreement with MK-PF-F-022 / MK-PF-F-034.

formula_checks.name: periodReturnSince
formula_checks.why: Latest close ÷ the close on or before the purchase day − 1 is right for a window that starts at a purchase (the purchase day's close is the nearest market price to the buy). The fallback is wrong for the same reason as MK-PF-F-029: when the prices begin after the purchase date it uses the first close on record, so 'since you bought it' quietly becomes 'since our prices begin'. Note also: it is never turned into a yearly rate, so in a 2Y window a holding bought 18 months ago shows an 18-month total beside other holdings' yearly rates (MK-PF-F-010 annualises 2Y); the finding on mixing the two is on MK-PF-F-014.
formula_checks.should_be: Latest close ÷ the close on or before the given date − 1; nothing when there is no close on or before that date.
formula_checks.rests_on: Agreement with MK-PF-F-034 and MK-PF-F-022; brief: a percent given when the starting value was never known.

formula_checks.name: closeAsOf
formula_checks.why: The last close on or before the target is right. The fallback is not: when every price is later than the target, it returns the FIRST close on record, i.e. a price from after the day asked. Any return built on it then covers a shorter span than the period it is labelled with — a period reaching back further than the record (shape 4) silently measured from the record's first day. MK-PF-F-034 (closeOnOrBefore) does the same job with no fallback and returns nothing; the two disagree for the same input. MK-PF-F-022 (factorOverMonths) also refuses in that case.
formula_checks.should_be: The close of the last price on or before the target; nothing when there is none (as MK-PF-F-034).
formula_checks.rests_on: Agreement with MK-PF-F-034 and MK-PF-F-022; brief: a percent given when the starting value was never known.

formula_checks.name: closeOnOrBefore
formula_checks.why: The last close on or before a day, and nothing when there is none, is the honest lookup: it never borrows a later price. It is what MK-PF-F-029 (closeAsOf) should do and does not — that card falls back to the first close; the finding is on MK-PF-F-029. Like MK-PF-F-009 it assumes the history is in date order; a sorted input is assumed in these cases.
